correctness.rationale: For each prime-power q>=3 and 4<=n<=q+1, pairwise nonproportional forms L_i:F_q²→F_q give bijective pair maps and hence q² distinct facets sharing pairwise at most one vertex. Every nonroot subset B of size >=2 is contained in a unique row facet, so descending-size elementary free-face pair removals B⊂B∪{(0,L_0(z))} are valid, orbitwise T-equivariant and leave exactly K_{q,(n-1)q}. The terminal connected graph has nq vertices and (n-1)q² edges, so H_1 rank (n-1)q²-nq+1. Its chain modules are C_1=(n-1)C[T], C_0=⊕_i C[T/ker L_i], H_0=1; taking characters yields m(1)=0, m(χ)=n-2 on selected nontrivial character lines and n-1 outside. For t≠0, at most one L_i vanishes, giving traces 1-q or 1 as stated. All claims follow from finite-field linear algebra for every prime power, with independent finite prime-field q=3,5 n=4 collapse/trace checks showing rank 16 and 56; no finite-to-infinite inference.
